about.title: Driven by
about.intro: I’m Jonathan David Rosenblatt, a software developer, Computer Engineer, and teaching assistant for Software Engineering I at FIUBA.
paragraphs: I love computing and Linux. My interests span backend development, algorithms, and the systems underneath the software.
My everyday favorites include gcc and i3. The projects here range from APIs and data models to a multiplayer game and machine learning.
about.journeyIntro: My work at FIUBA, on both sides of the classroom.
about.graduationDescription: I graduated in August 2026. My studies and teaching share the same focus: understanding problems and turning that understanding into working software.

projects.title: The project
projects.intro: Backend systems, games, and experiments. Some projects, from data models and APIs to local multiplayer and machine learning.

entries.title: Numi
entries.description: Gamification Platform for Recognition and Rewards in the Workplace
notes: A platform for workplace recognition and rewards through gamification.
The documented stack combines NestJS and PostgreSQL with Docker, Jest and Cypress.

entries.title: Wolfenstein 3D
notes: A team project for Taller de Programación I at FIUBA, with separate server and client executables and a map editor.
The repository documents GNU/Linux setup, SDL 2.0 and Qt5 dependencies, and scripts for installation and map management.

entries.title: Machine Learning Competition
entries.description: Predicting building damages after an earthquake.
notes: Predicting building damage after an earthquake using Python and the scientific computing ecosystem.
The project lists Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn and Jupyter; the repository identifies this as a team project.

entries.title: Goodreads Backend
entries.description: Goodreads imitation with auth, book management, news, notifications, questions, quotes, readings and users
notes: Authentication and book management alongside news, notifications, questions, quotes, readings and users.
Built with NestJS, Drizzle and PostgreSQL; the project lists Swagger for API documentation.

entries.title: MS Teams Notifier
entries.description: Simple Python program for people that can’t log in on their phones, that notifies you whenever a Microsoft Teams notification appears on your PC.
notes: A Python utility for forwarding desktop notifications when Microsoft Teams cannot be used on the phone.
The README describes Pushbullet setup, Windows notification integration and an extensible notification-provider interface.

entries.title: User CRUD
entries.description: Basic Spring CRUD with user creation, following, auth, persistence and management. Built in the PRE-AI era ;)
notes: User creation, following, authentication, persistence and management using Spring and Hibernate.
The README documents a shared Docker network, Docker Compose startup and a Flask-based mock frontend.
